query: Controlling for priority and category, which underlying causes explain longer resolution times?

per_column.name: resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: This is the dependent variable of the query -- resolution time. Derivable from opened_at and closed_at/sys_updated_on, both present. Values are sound readings of timestamps. Directly essential for the analysis.

per_column.name: issue_type
per_column.rationale: Categorises the underlying cause from short_description (VPN->connectivity, database->database, email->email). This is exactly the 'underlying causes' axis the query asks about, distinct from the coarse original category column. Row evidence shows sound extraction.

per_column.name: assignment_group_mismatch
per_column.rationale: A plausible driver of longer resolution (misrouting) and a genuine new axis. Groundedness is moderate: it presumably compares assignment_group vs closed_by/resolver group, which is derivable, but the exact rule is opaque and the sample row (email, mismatch=1) cannot be independently verified from shown text.

per_column.name: resolver_is_assignee
per_column.rationale: Compares assigned_to vs closed_by -- both original columns present, so derivable. A reasonable operational driver of delay. Somewhat overlapping conceptually with assignment_group_mismatch but offers a distinct row-level axis.

per_column.name: resolution_hours_vs_group_median
per_column.rationale: Largely a transform of resolution_hours (deviation from assignment_group median), so partially redundant with an added column. It can aid within-group comparison, but the query already asks to control for priority/category rather than group. Values derivable but heavily dependent on internal aggregation.

per_column.name: opened_hour
per_column.rationale: Cleanly derived from opened_at. Time-of-day could plausibly relate to resolution time (off-hours queueing), giving a mild new axis, but it is generic and not an 'underlying cause' in the causal sense the query targets.

per_column.name: opened_on_weekend
per_column.rationale: Derived from opened_at, well grounded. Weekend openings plausibly extend resolution due to reduced staffing -- a legitimate, if secondary, explanatory axis distinct from the raw hour.

judge.rationale: The set provides the target metric (resolution_hours), the key 'underlying cause' axis (issue_type), and several plausible operational/temporal drivers, all of which give real analytical leverage for explaining longer resolution times. Groundedness is generally strong: most columns are derivable from present timestamps and identity/group fields, with issue_type well supported by short_description evidence. Weaker spots are the routing/mismatch flags (opaque derivation rules, hard to verify from samples) and resolution_hours_vs_group_median (partly redundant transform of resolution_hours). No clear hallucinations observed in the provided row evidence.
